MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  September 12, 2017

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Pro Tem Sachs at 5:00 p.m., on September 12, 2017, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo,
California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on September 7, 2017, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Raths
  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs
  Mayor Bucknum (arrived at 5:15 p.m.)

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel - Anticipated Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph (4) of
  Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9 - One Potential Case.

CS2. Conference Involving a Joint Powers Agency - Orange County Fire Authority
  Discussion on Public Employee Appointment - Fire Chief, Government Code Section
  54957; Mayor Pro Tem Sachs - City Representative.

City Council Minutes  1  September 12, 2017
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:02 p.m., Mayor Pro Tem Sachs recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:00 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council addressed two Closed Session matters. They
received information and provided direction to staff but there was no reportable action.

INVOCATION: Council Member Raths

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Goodell

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Adopted Headquarters Battalion of the 1st Marine Division Quarterly Recognition

  Mayor Bucknum presented certificates of commendation to "Marine of the
  Quarter" Corporal Kevin Apencuxil. "Noncommissioned Officer of the Quarter" Sergeant
  Jose Eduardo Salcido was unable to attend the meeting.

P2.  Proclaim the Month of September 2017, as World Alzheimer’s Awareness Month

  Mayor Bucknum presented the proclamation to Sandy Lewis with the Alzheimer's
  Association of Orange County.

P3.  Recognize Hummus Bowl and YogaWorks as "Certified Green Businesses"

  Mayor Bucknum and Environmental Program Administrator Denise Matson presented a
  Certificate to the business owner of Hummus Bowl. YogaWorks will be recognized at
  another time.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Michael Dunbar, Tustin: stated that he is the General Manager of the Emerald Bay Service District
and Chair of Project Committee 15 which is the coalition that is in a contractual dispute with
Moulton Niguel Water District (MNWD) over non-payment of past due and current bills. He said
that MNWD forced Project Committee 15 to file litigation and MNWD has now has asked that the
jurisdiction for the trial be moved to downtown Los Angeles. Mr. Dunbar stated that this action
is not compatible with MNWD’s mantra of “open and transparent.”

Don Schone, M.V.: expressed concern that Mission Viejo doctors are failing to inform their breast
cancer patients that there is a casual relationship between breast and ovarian cancers and that there
is a new and simple early warning blood test.

City Council Minutes  2  September 12, 2017
 The following expressed concern with fraudulent business practices at Saatcchi Jewelry in Mission
Viejo and asked how they can be compensated for their judgments against Saatchi: Lara Alade,
M.V.; Robert Hardebeck, Long Beach; and Pamela St. Pierre, M.V.

Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: discussed a letter he wrote a Sheriff Hutchens entitled "If you see
something, say something." He said he reported party activities at Cordova Park and the Orange
County Sheriff’s Department did nothing so residents are banding together to take back their park.

Ayesha Medve, M.V.: requested that a street light be added to the connector road between
Barbadanes and Ambia/Celanova to maintain the walkability and safety of the neighborhood.

Ryan Farsai, M.V.: presented what he says is evidence that the City is illegally operating an
electronic sign on his property at La Paz and Marguerite. He asked the City to pay $1,000 per
month to lease the space or move the marquee to another corner.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 2, 6 and 13 were removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

3.  Check Register Dated August 11, 2017 in the Amount of $2,524,778.99

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated August 18, 2017 in the Amount of $951,252.00

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Check Register Dated August 25, 2017 in the Amount of $2,620,985.73

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

City Council Minutes  3  September 12, 2017
 7.  Community Development Financing Authority (CDFA) Treasurer’s Annual Report
  for Fiscal Year 2016-17 and Annual Review of the CDFA Investment Policy

  (1) Received and filed the accompanying Treasurer's Annual Report for Fiscal Year 2016-
  17; and (2) adopted CDFA Resolution 17-02 Approving the Authority's Investment Policy
  for FY 2017-18.

8.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority Treasurer’s Annual Report for Fiscal Year 2016-17
  and Annual Review of the Mission Viejo Housing Authority Investment Policy

  (1) Received and filed the accompanying Treasurer's Annual Report for Fiscal Year 2016-
  17; and (2) adopted Housing Authority Resolution 17-03 Approving the Mission Viejo
  Housing Authority Investment Policy for FY2017-18.

9.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for July 2017

  Received and filed.

10.  Mission Viejo Community Development  Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for July 2017

  Received and filed.

11.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for July 2017

  Received and filed.

12.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for July 2017

  Received and filed.

14.  Document Management System Software and Hardware Upgrade

  Approved agreement with Hyland Software and issuance of purchase order in the amount
  of $75,750 for purchase of OnBase software licensing and implementation.

15.  Geographic Information System (GIS) Renewal

  Approved entering into a 1-year agreement with Digital Map Products; and approved
  issuance of purchase order to Digital Map Products for 2017-18 services in the amount of
  $44,540.

16.  Resolution Amending the Employer-Employee Relations Procedures and Repealing
  Resolution No. 89-99

City Council Minutes  4  September 12, 2017
   Adopted Resolution 17-40 Establishing an Amended Employer-Employee Relations
  Resolution and repealing Resolution No. 89-99.

17.  Transmittal of Pre-PARE Trustee Reports for the quarter ending June 30, 2017

  Received and filed the accompanying Pre-PARE Trustee Reports for the Quarter ending
  June 30, 2017.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

6.  City Treasurer’s Annual Report for Fiscal Year 2016-17

  Shari Freidenrich, Orange County Treasurer-Tax Collector, provided information on the
  Orange County Investment Pool.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Mayor Bucknum, to (1) receive and
  file the accompanying City Treasurer's Annual Report for fiscal year 2016-2017; (2) adopt
  Resolution 17-38 Approving the City's Investment Policy for FY 2017-18; (3) set the
  Benchmark Index for FY 2017-18 to be a Government Securities Index comprised of 60%
  three-month Treasury Bills; 25% Treasury and Agency securities with maturities greater
  than one year and up to three years; and 15% Treasury and Agency securities with
  maturities greater than three years and up to five years; (4) adopt Resolution 17-39
  Authorizing the Deposit and Investment of Excess Funds with the Treasurer-Tax Collector
  of the County of Orange, California; and (5) authorize the Mayor to execute Agreement
  for the Deposit and Investment of Excess Funds into the County Treasury.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

2.  City Council Minutes

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: stated that once again, the Minutes reflect what city hall wants
  reflected. She suggested that speakers whose comments were not appreciated received less
  narrative than those who agree with city hall.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Raths, to approve
  the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of August 22, 2017, as presented.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
City Council Minutes  5  September 12, 2017
 13.  Ordinance Amending and Adding Various Sections to the Mission Viejo Municipal
  Code relating to Administrative Appeals, Signage, City Manager Authority, Code
  Interpretation/Maintenance, City Commission Terms, City Property/Right-of-Way
  Use, Community Safety, Water Quality, Grading, and Animal Control

  The following expressed various concerns with the amendments to the Mission Viejo
  Municipal Code including matters involving the homeless and the number of amendments
  included: Staycie Sena with her son Liam, M.V.; Julie Crandall, M.V. (Legal Aid Society
  of Orange County); Cathy Schlicht, M.V.; Ugochi Anaebere-Nicholson, Public Law
  Center, Santa Ana; Eve Garrow, American Civil Liberties Union, Santa Ana.

  The following expressed support for the ordinance and stated that there have been
  unfounded accusations against the City of Mission Viejo regarding the homeless: Robert
  Breton, M.V.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, to adopt
  Ordinance 17-324 Amending Sections 1.02.018, 1.03.018, 9.29.155, 9.29.220, 9.29.215,
  9.45.035, 2.08.060, 1.01.010, 1.01.005, 2.06.060, 13.04.010, 13.04.030, 13.04.050,
  12.08.030, 6.65.110, 8.10.600, 8.10.610, 14.03.020, 14.03.150, 14.03.330, 10.01.070,
  10.01.210, and 10.01.216, and Adding Section 14.20.90, Section 14.24.040, Section
  14.24.050, Section 1.01.171, and Division 4 Of Chapter 10.01, of The Mission Viejo
  Municipal Code Relating to Administrative Appeals, Signage, City Manager Authority,
  Code Interpretation/Maintenance, City Commission Terms, City Property/Right-Of-Way
  Use, Community Safety, Water Quality, Grading, and Animal Control.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

18.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs presented the report.

19.  Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

20.  Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  Mayor Bucknum presented the report.

21.  Economic Development Ad-Hoc Committee Report
City Council Minutes  6  September 12, 2017
   Director of Community Development Elaine Lister presented a staff report.

  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs and Council Member Goodell commented on recent activity with
  the Economic Development Ad-Hoc Committee.

STAFF REPORTS

22.  Orange County Sheriff’s Department (OCSD) Update

  Lt. Ken Binning presented the report.

23.  City Goals and Objectives in Wireless Telecommunications/Video/Video
  Service/Cable Contracts and Consulting Services

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  Dick Ackerman, 5 Bars, Irvine: provided background on Senate Bill 649, stating that the
  bill will basically take away the majority of local control as to where small cell sites will
  go. He said that his company is trying to offer cities some protection from SB 649.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Mayor Bucknum, to authorize staff
  to review consulting services to determine if these services are available, and the price and
  terms related thereto.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

24.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell discussed his attendance at the Orange County Forum’s 2018 Housing
Outlook Report. He said it was very interesting and he was reminded that cities have to be as
proactive and creative as possible to establish opportunities for affordable housing so people can
live and work here. He also attended Supervisor Lisa Bartlett’s South County Homeless
Roundtable where the same issue came up - a lack of housing - and a recent survey of Orange
County residents put that at the top of their list of concerns for the first time ever. Council Member
City Council Minutes  7  September 12, 2017
 Goodell said that South County cities are working together, along with the County and service
organizations, to serve the population and find solutions that work for everybody. He noted that
the topic of homelessness came up at the Council Meeting two weeks ago and on the same
meeting’s agenda, the Treasurers Report reflected the City’s payment for the two transitional
housing units that were purchased in partnership with Families Forward. Council Member Goodell
stated that it’s important to remember that the City is doing as much as it can and he hopes that the
people who have come out to advocate for the homeless will participate in the ongoing discussions
to find solutions. He suggested they get on Supervisor Bartlett’s mailing list so they will know
when her quarterly Homeless Roundtables are taking place.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley expressed her gratitude and commendation for the effort that was put out
for the Patriot Day remembrance ceremony yesterday. She thanked Boy Scout Troop 1602 for
their work in presenting the colors and the flag ceremony, and Division Chief John Abel who
spoke very eloquently of what it was like on 9/11/2005 for first responders all over the country.
Chief Abel shared what goes through the mind of a firefighter and remembered those who lost
their lives, both victims and rescuers. Council Member Kelley noted that a Mission Viejo resident
was a member of the Urban Search and Rescue Task Force 5 which went to Houston after
Hurricane Harvey. The team of about 45 members left and didn't know how long they'd be gone
but while they were there they rescued more than 1,000 people. This responder’s wife told Council
Member Kelley that she was happy that her husband was able to go and do something that he
loves, which is to help others. In closing, Council Member Kelley announced that the Community
of Character word for the month of September is responsibility and she shared some of the
associated character traits.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths said that he wanted to clear up some comments made by Mayor Pro Tem
Sachs. He expressed that he thinks very highly of City staff and all the work they do and he would
never put them down for anything. He noted that he is just a little frustrated on the issue of the
Village Center and he offered his help in getting the Vision Plan projects to move forward. He
said that it’s 14 months away from an election and 3½ years ago he promised the constituents that
the City would get something going. Council Member Raths commented on Mayor Pro Tem Sachs
recent newsletter which claimed that he voted no, without making a comment, on the resolution
supporting the Transportation Corridor Agencies’ efforts to relieve traffic congestion. Council
Member Raths said that the video tape of the meeting shows that he made several comments about
his no vote including that he did not want the two cities (Mission Viejo and San Clemente) to get
into a war and he’d rather bring them together. He said he felt a non-binding resolution was not
relevant at the time. Council Member Raths announced that Supervisor Lisa Bartlett nominated
him to serve the 5th District as the Veterans Advisory Councilman and he looks forward to
representing the veterans in South County. He also noted that on September 19 from 10:00 a.m. to
1:00 p.m. Supervisor Bartlett will host an Operation Veterans Success event in the quad area in
front of the Veterans Memorial at Saddleback College. Referencing a public comment earlier in
the meeting about a homeless Veteran, Council Member Raths shared that there is an amazing
Veterans Shelter in Tustin that takes care of veterans by providing barracks, gardens and jobs. In
City Council Minutes  8  September 12, 2017
 closing, he discussed his attendance at the Hometown Heroes banner program event in San
Clemente where he and his colleagues had a great time representing the City.

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs provided an update on the seven-member group from Orange County Fire
Authority which is in Florida to help with disaster relief efforts. Five are incident management
team members, one is a search dog handler and the group also includes a structural engineer. He
said that the County is well-represented in Florida and the City can be very proud of those efforts.
Mayor Pro Tem Sachs asked the City Clerk to give the backgammon set that was donated tonight
to the Library. Referring to the Cordova Park issue that was brought up earlier in the evening, he
advised residents to not take the law into their own hands, invite trouble or put themselves in
harm’s way. Mayor Pro Tem Sachs referenced a recent article in which he was quoted on police
services costs in Orange County and the City of Mission Viejo. He reminded his colleagues that
many times during budget deliberations he expressed concern that public safety costs continue to
escalate and that the City gets very little information from Orange County Sheriff’s Department
(OCSD) as to what the actual costs are. He said it has become more difficult for the Council to
understand and negotiate the contract when they don’t have a clear understanding of the expenses
required to support a deputy in the City. He also noted that the OCSD budget is managed by the
Orange County Board of Supervisors and the City has no input but it is saddled with the bills.
Mayor Pro Tem Sachs said he is going to continue to put pressure on folks to make sure that the
Council fully understands the cost of policing because, at the current rate of escalation, the City
will start to have expenses greater than revenues in about three years. He stated that without
additional data, it may be time to start a new police services JPA in South County because Mission
Viejo residents deserve the best that money can buy.

Mayor Bucknum

Mayor Bucknum echoed sentiments about the Patriots Day event yesterday. She said it was very
moving to see residents chalk message and the boards are now on display at City Hall for those
who want to stop by and see them. She thanked Congresswoman Mimi Walters for the recent
elected officials’ breakfast and she also attended the Orange County Business Council’s event that
provided an amazing and insightful look into Washington DC. Mayor Bucknum noted that the
American Heroes Tribute Banners are funded by a non-profit that raises money to pay for the
banners and the frames that hold them and a copy is always given to the family of the deceased
soldier. Referencing a memo from South County Outreach, she shared that Mission Viejo residents
have provided food pantry services for 738 people in town. Mayor Bucknum provided reminders
of upcoming events including the Library's 20th Anniversary on Saturday, October 14; the Tee it
Up Fore Marines golf tournament on October 13; Casta Del Sol’s 45th anniversary celebration; and
the Mission Viejo Country Club 50th anniversary event on September 23. She said there are a lot
of milestones happening in Mission Viejo and next year, the Mission Viejo Nadadores will
celebrate their 50th anniversary from June 15-17, 2018, following the completion of the Marguerite
Aquatics Complex. Mayor Bucknum thanked Mayor Pro Tem Sachs and Council Member Goodell
for their work on the Economic Development Committee. She said there is a lot of work being
done and sometimes it is hard to see what is happening behind the scenes. She expressed
appreciation to Council Member Raths for his offer to help and suggested the Council hold a public
City Council Minutes  9  September 12, 2017
 meeting to talk about what the City is working on. Finally, referencing the toll road matter, Mayor
Bucknum said that the Council Members do care and want to work with other cities but Mission
Viejo residents want to know what their City's position is. She said that the Council will continue
to work collaboratively with neighboring cities, to be solution-oriented, and the City's letter to the
Transportation Corridor Agency expressed support for a north-south route.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:11 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Bucknum adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, September 26, 2017, at 5:00 p.m.

____________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of September 26, 2017

City Council Minutes  10  September 12, 2017
